answer: Exit should be priced by history. Each identity accrues an audit bond sized to its lifetime payouts — the ledger's kernel record of all earnings — locked through an audit window after the last claim. Leaving cheaply is impossible: a clone farm mass-claiming for months posts bonds on every key at once, under crystal-clear public accounting of who earned what. Late-proven fraud burns the bond retroactively, striking the vertex of accumulated value where it hurts. Honest agents redeem at maturity untouched. The bigger the past, the larger the guarantee — scale becomes collateral, not profit.
